questions.question: How can the energy provided by a food sample burned under a tube of water be calculated?
options: Energy (J) = mass of water (g) × rise in temperature (°C) × 4.2
Energy (J) = mass of food (g) × rise in temperature (°C) × 4.2
Energy (J) = mass of water (g) + rise in temperature (°C) × 100
Energy (J) = volume of water (ml) × mass of food (g) / 4.2

questions.question: Which two measurements of a person are required to calculate their Body Mass Index (BMI)?
options: Height and waist circumference
Body mass and age
Height and body mass
Body mass and body fat percentage

questions.question: What is the primary cause of a deficiency disease in humans?
options: Consuming too much dietary fat and sugar
Not consuming enough of a particular nutrient
An infection caused by a pathogen
A lack of regular physical exercise

questions.question: What does the term "recovery time" refer to in relation to physical exercise?
options: The total duration of a vigorous exercise session
The time it takes for a person to fall asleep after working out
The time it takes for the heart rate to return to its resting rate after exercise
The time required for muscles to double their strength after training

questions.question: How does a person's physical fitness level typically affect their recovery time after exercise?
options: Fitter individuals have a shorter recovery time.
Fitter individuals have a longer recovery time.
Physical fitness has no impact on recovery time.
Fitter individuals do not experience a recovery phase.

questions.question: Why do breathing rate and heart rate increase during physical exercise?
options: To transport excess carbon dioxide to the muscles for energy production
To supply cells with more oxygen needed for increased cellular respiration
To decrease the body temperature by reducing blood flow to the lungs
To prevent glucose from entering the active muscle cells

questions.question: When investigating the effect of different types of exercise on heart rate, which of the following should be kept as control variables to ensure a fair test?
options: The room temperature and the type of footwear worn only
The heart rate before exercise and the heart rate after exercise
The person performing the exercise and the length of time spent exercising
The age of the person and the time of day they eat breakfast

questions.question: Why might a teenager have different nutritional requirements compared to an elderly office worker?
options: Nutrient requirements are determined solely by genetics and never change with age.
People need different amounts of particular nutrients at different stages of life depending on their lifestyle.
Teenagers require fewer carbohydrates because they do not grow as rapidly as elderly adults.
Elderly adults require significantly more protein to build new bone structures.

questions.question: Which two units of measurement are commonly used on food labels to compare the amount of energy provided by food?
options: Grams and milligrams
Kilojoules and calories
Watts and joules
Degrees Celsius and Newtons

questions.question: Besides providing energy, what is another major role of food in the human body?
options: To act as a direct replacement for nervous system impulses
To serve as a source of building materials to make biomass for growth and repair
To physically lubricate the joints using consumed dietary water
To filter harmful gases from the respiratory system

questions.question: Which of the following is a major health issue that has an increased risk of development associated with obesity?
options: Heart disease
Scurvy
Color blindness
Genetic mutations

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only recognized food groups required by the human body?
options: Protein, carbohydrate, lipids/fats, water, minerals, vitamins, and fibre
Protein, carbon dioxide, lipids/fats, oxygen, and glucose
Carbohydrate, calcium, iron, starch, and hormones
Vitamins, minerals, water, amino acids, and enzymes

questions.question: In a school laboratory experiment to compare the energy content of different foods, how is the energy released from burning food directly captured and measured?
options: By measuring the mass loss of the food sample using a balance
By burning the food to heat a volume of water and measuring the water's temperature change
By measuring the volume of oxygen gas consumed by the burning food
By recording the duration of the flame using a stopwatch

questions.question: If you plot a bar chart showing how different types of exercise (such as walking, running, and cycling) affect heart rate, where should the types of exercise be placed?
options: On the y-axis, because they represent continuous numerical data
On the x-axis, because the independent variable is categoric data
In a separate table, as categoric data cannot be plotted on a bar chart
On both axes to show the average values

questions.question: How can symptoms of ill health be identified in an individual?
options: Only by performing advanced genetic sequencing in a laboratory
By observing changes in normal body appearance, function, and behaviour
By checking if the person's height increases over time
By measuring the exact mass of food they consume in a single meal
